rationale: SMB website owners and SEO freelancers deal with indexing failures regularly and there is a real market for diagnostic tools (Ahrefs, Screaming Frog, and IndexNow services all attract paid users), giving moderate willingness to pay. However, buyer clarity sits at 5 — the segment spans consumer bloggers who pay nothing to SEO agencies with real budgets, and the signal doesn't clearly point to a named business buyer. Buildability and operational autonomy are solid (7 each): a Claude-powered site audit that ingests a URL, crawls accessible pages, checks canonicals, content quality signals, internal linking, and outputs a prioritised indexing action plan is shippable without custom infra. Total of 5.6 clears validate but buyer_clarity (5) falls short of the build gate floor of 6, correctly capping this at validate.
solution_plan: (1) WHAT: An on-demand Google indexing diagnostic report — a user submits their site URL and gets a prioritised PDF/HTML report explaining why their posts aren't indexed and what to fix, generated by Claude. (2) BUILD: The factory builds a simple intake form (URL + email + optional GSC export upload), Claude analyses the site structure and content signals, and outputs a structured report; delivery via email with a Stripe payment link ($29–$49 one-time per report). No operator coding needed. (3) SELL: Target SEO freelancers and content-site owners via Reddit (r/SEO, r/juststart), Indie Hackers, and Twitter/X search for 'google not indexing'; factory drafts outreach posts and DMs for operator approval before sending. (4) MAINTAIN: Report generation is fully automated; billing via Stripe; support queries answered by Claude via a simple email forwarding rule; operator approves outreach batches only. (5) VALIDATE FIRST: Before building, post a manual offer in 2–3 SEO communities offering a free diagnostic to 5 sites in exchange for feedback — if 10+ people respond in 48 hours, the demand signal is real enough to build.
notes: build_gate buyer_clarity unmet: scored 5, floor is 6. Validate by sharpening ICP to 'SEO freelancers billing clients' or 'Shopify store owners with content blogs' — both have clearer budget authority than generic 'website owners'.
